account: UNEP states that its Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) combines satellite observations, scientific review and AI to identify emissions for government and company action. UNEP’s MARS mitigation index lists eight Turkmenistan cases: two in Yelguyi in November 2024, Babarap in June 2025, Gugurtli field in July 2025, Balguyy in August 2025, two in Dauletabad in February 2026, and Lebap Province in March 2026. Each entry has a source identifier and a link to an individual case document. UNEP describes these as mitigations that its notification and monitoring system helped prompt and verify. UNEP's document for case TKM_S_406, updated on 15 April 2026, states that MARS first detected the Lebap pipeline leak on 22 June 2025. It states that MARS estimated 16,000 tonnes of methane from 47 plumes. The document reports that the operator repaired a corroded flowline and that satellites detected no further emissions after 7 March 2026. The Guardian reported on 31 August 2026 that the first Turkmen leak had been fixed in November 2024. It reported that Turkmenistan had stopped eight leaks by repairing corroded pipes, faulty wells and failing flares. The MARS program manager told the Guardian that Turkmenistan's response rate was growing month by month. She added that eight cases did not yet change the overall magnitude of Turkmen emissions. The available aggregate evidence does not isolate the contribution of AI from that of analysts, notifications and physical repairs, and it does not quantify their combined benefit.

fields.account: UNEP states that its Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) combines satellite observations, scientific review and AI to identify emissions for government and company action. UNEP’s MARS mitigation index lists eight Turkmenistan cases: two in Yelguyi in November 2024, Babarap in June 2025, Gugurtli field in July 2025, Balguyy in August 2025, two in Dauletabad in February 2026, and Lebap Province in March 2026. Each entry has a source identifier and a link to an individual case document. UNEP describes these as mitigations that its notification and monitoring system helped prompt and verify. UNEP's document for case TKM_S_406, updated on 15 April 2026, states that MARS first detected the Lebap pipeline leak on 22 June 2025. It states that MARS estimated 16,000 tonnes of methane from 47 plumes. The document reports that the operator repaired a corroded flowline and that satellites detected no further emissions after 7 March 2026. The Guardian reported on 31 August 2026 that the first Turkmen leak had been fixed in November 2024. It reported that Turkmenistan had stopped eight leaks by repairing corroded pipes, faulty wells and failing flares. The MARS program manager told the Guardian that Turkmenistan's response rate was growing month by month. She added that eight cases did not yet change the overall magnitude of Turkmen emissions. The available aggregate evidence does not isolate the contribution of AI from that of analysts, notifications and physical repairs, and it does not quantify their combined benefit.
